# table

```go
import "github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/table"
```

Package table sizes columns to their contents and lays cells out in them: a row is as narrow as its widest values allow, and when even that is too wide, the columns give way in a declared order rather than all at once.

## Constants

<a name="Gap"></a>Gap is the columns between cells.

```go
const Gap = 2
```

<a name="Fit"></a>
## func [Fit](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/table/table.go#L27>)

```go
func Fit(cols []Column, rows [][]string, width int) []int
```

Fit returns each column's width: its widest cell \(title included\) capped at Max, then shrunk to fit width \- Flex first down to Min, then the widest, never below minCell. Min is a floor for shrinking, not a width to grow to.

<a name="Row"></a>
## func [Row](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/table/table.go#L85>)

```go
func Row(widths []int, cells []string) string
```

Row lays cells out in widths, padded to their columns and separated by Gap; the last cell is cut but not padded, so the row ends where it ends.

<a name="Titles"></a>
## func [Titles](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/table/table.go#L102>)

```go
func Titles(cols []Column, widths []int) string
```

Titles is the header row: every column's title in its width.

<a name="Column"></a>
## type [Column](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/bezel/blob/main/table/table.go#L15-L19>)

Column declares one column; Min and Max bound its width \(0 = unbounded\). Flex marks the column that shrinks first: a truncated name is still recognisable, a truncated version is not.

```go
type Column struct {
    Title    string
    Min, Max int
    Flex     bool
}
```
